summary.text: This opportunity briefing explores combining Gaussian processes, Kolmogorov-Arnold networks, and regression to achieve scalable probabilistic predictions and uncertainty quantification. Standard Kolmogorov-Arnold networks lack probabilistic outputs and exact Gaussian process extensions scale cubically with dataset size N. Integrating sparse variational Gaussian processes into the Kolmogorov-Arnold network topology using inducing points and analytic moment matching reduces computational complexity and enables scalable probabilistic predictions for regression tasks.

target_user.text: The target users include corporate assignees and academic researchers working on automated road modeling, manufacturing anomaly detection, wireless signal processing, video tracking, and soft sensing models.

jtbd.text: Perform regression tasks that require scalable probabilistic predictions and uncertainty quantification.

value_prop.text: Integrates sparse variational Gaussian processes into the Kolmogorov-Arnold network topology using inducing points and analytic moment matching to reduce computational complexity and enable scalable probabilistic predictions for regression tasks.

riskiest_assumption.text: The feasibility score (axis F score: 3.0) indicates that analytic moment matching and sparse variational inference over the edge-wise univariate functions of Kolmogorov-Arnold networks may fail to preserve well-calibrated epistemic uncertainty at scale.

mvp.text: Build a technical proof of concept that implements a sparse variational Gaussian process over a Kolmogorov-Arnold network using existing Python packages to test scalability and uncertainty calibration on a benchmark regression task.
mvp.type: technical proof of concept from existing packages

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold of negative log-likelihood below a baseline MLP on held-out regression data while maintaining quasi-linear scaling with respect to sample size N.

kill_criteria.text: If training complexity exceeds a proposed threshold of cubic scaling with sample size N, or if epistemic uncertainty calibration degrades significantly compared to exact Gaussian processes, the approach should be abandoned.

open_source.use: Used for evaluating the calibration of predictive uncertainty on regression outputs.

Used for surrogate modeling tasks to benchmark regression accuracy.

to_build.text: Implement the analytic moment matching layer that integrates sparse variational Gaussian process inducing points directly into the edge-wise univariate activation functions of Kolmogorov-Arnold networks.
